key_insight: The paper shows that Rust’s ownership model plus Aeneas can turn production cryptographic code into Lean-friendly pure models, enabling scalable machine-checked verification.
engineering_relevance: This approach verifies real high-performance crypto software without rewriting it for proof, making it practical for secure, portable deployment across platforms.
method: Extract Rust code into Lean with Aeneas to avoid low-level pointer and aliasing reasoning.
Use Lean tactics/libraries and AI-assisted proof generation to discharge most formal proofs.
Apply the toolchain to SymCrypt code and extensions including SHA-3, ML-KEM, FrodoKEM, ML-DSA, and HPKE.
evidence_signal: The authors report a 237KLOC Lean development verifying safety, panic-freedom, and functional correctness for 16.7KLOC of Rust code across x86-64 and ARM.
watch_item: The approach still depends on expert design and review for standards formalization and platform-specific intrinsics, which remain harder to automate.
paper_title: Scaling Verification of Cryptographic Software with Aeneas, Rust, and Lean
